mainTopic: Why a פסח slaughtered for another purpose becomes a שלמים, and the פסוקים that teach it
overview: This amud asks why a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose turns into a שלמים specifically. One answer is that an offering any Jew may eat can only switch to another offering any Jew may eat. A second answer, from רבי יוסי ברבי אבין, is that a קדשים קלים offering can only switch to another קדשים קלים offering. The גמרא then asks why the פסח could not become a מעשר, a בכור, a תמורה, or a תודה instead. פסוקים limit מעשר, בכור and תמורה to the real thing. A תודה's bread is ruled out because a leftover תודה itself brings no bread. Next the גמרא tests the פסוק 'if his offering is from the flock' as the source that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים, and defends it against several challenges. Finally it notes that three different פסוקים seem to teach this same rule, and it begins to explain why all three are needed. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An eaten offering switches only to another eaten offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers why a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose becomes a שלמים: an offering that is eaten can only be switched to another offering that is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Offerings that are eaten get switched over to offerings that are eaten. But offerings that are eaten do not get switched over to offerings that are not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why does a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose turn into a שלמים and not, for example, an עולה? The answer is that an eaten offering only switches to another eaten offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח is eaten, and so is a שלמים. An עולה is burned completely and nobody eats it. So the פסח can 'land' on a שלמים but not on an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: We switch it over; its status is pushed over to another kind of offering
Offerings that are eaten
Toward, to (here: switched over to)
The Pesach offering

phrases.english: Offerings that are eaten are diverted
phrases.notes: 'Diverted' means the offering's status gets switched to a different kind of offering. Here it is talking about the פסח.

phrases.english: to offerings that are eaten,
but offerings that are eaten are not diverted
to offerings that are not eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹחִין קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִים אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section: why a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose becomes a שלמים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An eaten offering switches only to another eaten offering, so the פסח becomes a שלמים and not an עולה.

steps.title: But a חטאת and an אשם are eaten too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a חטאת and an אשם are also eaten, so why doesn't the פסח become one of them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that a חטאת and an אשם are not eaten?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 1 by pointing out that חטאת and אשם are also eaten offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only rule is 'eaten goes to eaten,' then the פסח could just as easily become a חטאת or an אשם, since the כהנים eat those. So 'being eaten' alone cannot explain why it becomes a שלמים specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (opens a surprised challenge)
Sin offering
Guilt offering
Are eaten

phrases.english: Is that to say that a sin offering and a guilt offering
are not eaten?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם מִי לָא מִיתְאַכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an eaten offering switches to another eaten offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חטאת and אשם are also eaten, so the rule does not explain why the פסח becomes a שלמים specifically.

steps.title: Offerings eaten by everyone switch only to offerings eaten by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the answer: an offering that anyone may eat switches only to another offering that anyone may eat, which means a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: offerings eaten by every person are switched to offerings eaten by every person. But offerings eaten by every person are not switched to offerings that are not eaten by every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer by making the rule more precise: it matters who eats the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any Jew may eat a פסח, and the same is true of a שלמים. A חטאת and an אשם are eaten only by male כהנים. So the פסח matches only the שלמים, and the challenge from step 2 is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected version)
By every person, meaning any Jew, not only כהנים
Peace offering, which any Jew may eat
Priests

steps.whatToRemember: The key match is who eats it: a פסח (eaten by anyone) can only become a שלמים (eaten by anyone), not a חטאת or אשם (eaten only by כהנים).

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דּוֹחִין קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְכׇל אָדָם
phrases.english: Rather, offerings that are eaten by every person are diverted
to offerings that are eaten by every person,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דּוֹחִין קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְכׇל אָדָם
phrases.english: but offerings that are eaten by every person are not diverted

phrases.aramaic: אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים שֶׁאֵין נֶאֱכָלִין לְכׇל אָדָם.
phrases.english: to offerings that are not eaten by every person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דּוֹחִין קָדָשִׁים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by refining the rule from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refinement of the rule (narrowing the category)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any eaten offering can receive the פסח's status, including חטאת and אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an offering eaten by any Jew, a שלמים, can receive it.

steps.title: A different answer based on levels of holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי אבין answers differently: a קדשים קלים offering switches only to another קדשים קלים offering, not to קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי the son of רבי אבין said: offerings of lighter holiness are switched to offerings of lighter holiness, but offerings of lighter holiness are not switched to offerings of the highest holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי אבין offers another way to explain why the פסח becomes a שלמים, using levels of holiness instead of who eats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח and a שלמים are both קדשים קלים, the lighter level of holiness. עולה, חטאת and אשם are all קדשי קדשים, the highest level. So the פסח can only move within its own level, which leaves the שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lighter holiness (like שלמים and פסח)
Offerings of the highest holiness (like עולה, חטאת, אשם)
Burnt offering, completely burned on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the same result: by who eats it (anyone, not only כהנים) or by level of holiness (קדשים קלים stays in קדשים קלים). Either way, the פסח becomes a שלמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Avin, says:

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹחִין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
phrases.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity are diverted to offerings of lesser sanctity,
but offerings of lesser sanctity are not diverted
to offerings of the most sacred order.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the original question, instead of the 'eaten by every person' rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative principle (level of holiness instead of who eats it)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח could become any eaten offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח stays within קדשים קלים, so it can only become a שלמים.

steps.title: Why not let the פסח become a מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר רבי סברין argues that under the קדשים קלים rule, a פסח slaughtered for the sake of מעשר should become a מעשר. That would make a real difference: it would need no נסכים, and selling it would earn lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר רבי סברין objects: Then say that if someone slaughtered the פסח as a מעשר, it should become a מעשר! What difference would that make? It would not need libations, and a person who sold it would get lashes for 'it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of רבי יוסי ברבי אבין from step 4. מעשר בהמה is also קדשים קלים, so why should the פסח become specifically a שלמים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'קדשים קלים switches only to קדשים קלים' leaves more than one choice open, and מעשר fits it too. The גמרא shows the question is not just theory. A מעשר needs no נסכים, while a שלמים does, and a מעשר may not be sold even after it is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (introduces a challenge)
The animal tithe: every tenth animal, which is holy
For what הלכה? What practical difference would it make?
Libations of wine, flour, and oil that come with certain offerings
'It shall not be redeemed': the ban on redeeming or selling מעשר

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rabbi Savrin objects to it:
phrases.notes: Some versions read the name as סבריו (in round brackets); the corrected name is the one in square brackets, סברין.

phrases.english: Say: if he slaughtered it for the sake of the tithe,
let it become a tithe!
For what halacha would that matter?
That it should not require libations,
and to give lashes for selling it, for violating 'it shall not be redeemed.'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. 'It shall not be redeemed' is from ויקרא 27:33.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי סַבְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי ברבי אבין's rule from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a קדשים קלים offering switches only to another קדשים קלים offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר is also קדשים קלים, so the rule does not explain why the פסח becomes specifically a שלמים and not a מעשר.

steps.title: Only the real tenth animal is a מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'the tenth shall be holy' teaches that only the actual tenth animal is a מעשר. No other animal can become one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The tenth shall be holy.' This one is a מעשר, and no other animal is a מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. מעשר status comes only from being the tenth animal counted, so a פסח cannot become a מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'the tenth' limits מעשר to the animal that was actually counted as tenth. A מעשר is created only by counting. Slaughtering a different animal 'for the sake of מעשר' cannot make it one, so מעשר drops out as a choice for the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The tenth shall be holy'
And no other animal is a tithe

phrases.english: The verse says: 'The tenth shall be holy':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:32

phrases.english: this one is a tithe, and no other is a tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any קדשים קלים offering, including מעשר, could be what the פסח becomes
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר is limited to the actual tenth animal, so the פסח cannot become a מעשר

steps.title: Why not let the פסח become a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסח slaughtered for the sake of a בכור does not become like a בכור. That would also make a difference: no נסכים, and it would be given to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say that if someone slaughtered the פסח as a בכור, it should be like a בכור! What difference would that make? It would not need libations, and it would also be given to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses again with another קדשים קלים offering, the בכור. The פסוק about מעשר does not seem to cover a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 removed only מעשר. A בכור is also קדשים קלים, so the same question comes back. The practical differences are that a בכור needs no נסכים and its meat goes to the כהנים, not to the owner as with a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
Alternatively; or also
The priests

phrases.english: Say: if he slaughtered it for the sake of a firstborn,
let it be like a firstborn!
For what halacha would that matter?
That it should not require libations,
or also that he should give it to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא שַׁחְטֵיהּ לְשֵׁם בְּכוֹר לֶיהֱוֵי כִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge from step 5 with a different offering that the answer in step 6 does not cover
steps.kashyaTarget: The קדשים קלים rule, which step 6 has not yet defended against the בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בכור is also קדשים קלים, and the 'tenth' פסוק limits only מעשר, so the פסח might become a בכור.

steps.title: A בכור is learned from מעשר through a shared word
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on the word 'passing,' found with both בכור and מעשר, teaches that a בכור is also limited to the real thing. So the פסח becomes neither one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בכור too: we learn it from מעשר through the shared word 'passing' (עברה) found in both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the בכור question. It applies the מעשר limit to בכור through a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses a form of the word 'pass' (עברה) for both בכור and מעשר. That shared word links the two topics. Just as only the real tenth animal is a מעשר, only a real firstborn is a בכור, so a פסח slaughtered for its sake does not become one.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both
'Passing': the shared word in the פסוקים about בכור and מעשר
He derives; it is learned

steps.whatToRemember: A פסח slaughtered for another purpose becomes a שלמים, not a מעשר or a בכור. מעשר is limited to the real tenth animal, and בכור is linked to it by the shared word 'passing.'

phrases.english: A firstborn too:
it is learned from the tithe through 'passing' and 'passing.'
phrases.notes: For בכור the word is in שמות 13:12, and for מעשר it is in ויקרא 27:32.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר נָמֵי עֲבָרָה עֲבָרָה מִמַּעֲשֵׂר גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by extending the answer of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה that extends an earlier limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בכור, being קדשים קלים and not covered by the 'tenth' פסוק, could be what the פסח becomes
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit on מעשר carries over to בכור, so the פסח becomes only a שלמים

steps.title: Why not let the פסח become a substitute offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if a פסח is slaughtered for the sake of a תמורה, it should become a תמורה. That would matter in practice, because of lashes and the ban on selling or redeeming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say: if someone slaughtered it for the sake of a substitute, it should become a substitute! What practical difference would that make? He would get lashes over it, or it would fall under 'it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge in the same pattern as the מעשר and בכור questions. It asks why a פסח slaughtered as a תמורה does not actually become a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After מעשר and בכור were ruled out, the גמרא tries the same question with תמורה: why shouldn't a פסח slaughtered as a תמורה actually become one? The גמרא shows this is not just a name game, because becoming a תמורה would bring lashes and a ban on selling or redeeming the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a consecrated animal. It becomes holy too.
'But say...': introduces a suggestion the גמרא wants to test
'For what הלכה?': what practical difference would it make?
To receive lashes over it
'It shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed': a ban on selling or redeeming

phrases.english: But say: if he slaughtered it for the sake of a substitute,
let it become a substitute!
For what halacha would it matter?
To receive lashes over it,
or also, so that it would stand under
'it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: שַׁחְטֵיהּ לְשֵׁם תְּמוּרָה – לֶיהֱוֵי תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מעשר and בכור were ruled out, the גמרא tries the same challenge with תמורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a פסח slaughtered for another קדשים קלים offering takes on that offering's identity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is general, it should apply to תמורה too. That would bring real consequences, like lashes and a ban on selling or redeeming it.

steps.title: Only a real substitute is a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן learns from the פסוק 'it and its substitute' that only the actual swapped animal is a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: The verse says, 'then it and its substitute shall be'. This one is a substitute, and no other animal is a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. Only an animal that was actually swapped can be a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'its substitute' points to one specific animal: the one used in the swap. So a פסח cannot become a תמורה just by being slaughtered for that purpose. This follows the same pattern as the מעשר and בכור answers: the category is limited to the real thing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is a substitute, and no other is a substitute

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said:
The verse says:
'then it and its substitute shall be [holy]',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33

phrases.english: this one is a substitute,
and no other animal is a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תמורה challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting derivation from a פסוק: the category is restricted to the real thing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח slaughtered for the sake of a תמורה becomes a תמורה, like other קדשים קלים switches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits תמורה to the animal actually swapped, so the פסח does not become a תמורה.

steps.title: Why not let the פסח become a thanks offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if a פסח is slaughtered for the sake of a תודה, it should become like a תודה and need loaves of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say: if he slaughtered it for the sake of a thanks offering, it should become like a thanks offering! What practical difference would that make? It would need to be brought with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more offering in the same pattern. It asks why a פסח slaughtered as a תודה does not become like a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is a קדשים קלים offering, so the switching rule seems to fit it well. The practical difference is that a תודה must be brought together with loaves of bread. So the question is whether this פסח would now need those loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering, a קדשים קלים offering brought with loaves of bread
To require it to be brought with bread

phrases.english: But say: if he slaughtered it for the sake of a thanks offering,
let it become like a thanks offering!
For what halacha would it matter?
To require it to be brought with bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: שַׁחְטֵיהּ לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה – לֶיהֱוֵי כִּי תוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After תמורה was ruled out, the גמרא tries the same challenge with תודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a פסח slaughtered for another קדשים קלים offering takes on that offering's identity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה is קדשים קלים, so by the rule the פסח should become a תודה and need bread.

steps.title: A leftover פסח cannot need more than a real פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a rhetorical question. A real פסח needs no bread, so it makes no sense for a leftover פסח to need bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing, where the פסח itself does not need bread, but its leftover does need bread?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the תודה challenge with a question that shows the idea is absurd. It is not really asking for information.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leftover פסח is an animal set aside as a פסח that was not offered in its proper time. It would be strange for this leftover to carry a stricter requirement, bread, than a real פסח on its proper day. So the פסח does not take on the bread requirement of a תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח: an animal set aside as a פסח but not offered in its proper time
'Is there such a thing?': a rhetorical question showing an idea is absurd
Itself, the real thing

steps.whatToRemember: A פסח slaughtered for another purpose does not become a מעשר, בכור, or תמורה, because פסוקים limit each of these to the real thing. It also does not need the bread of a תודה. Step 13 challenges the reason given here, and step 14 explains the reason properly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מי איכא מידי' as a real question. It is the answer: it shows that the suggestion makes no sense.

phrases.english: Is there such a thing
where the פסח itself does not need bread,
but its leftover does need bread?!
phrases.notes: 'Its leftover' means an animal set aside as a פסח that wasn't brought on time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּפֶסַח גּוּפֵיהּ לָא בָּעֵי לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תודה challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical answer by showing the result would be absurd
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח slaughtered for the sake of a תודה becomes like a תודה and needs bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: A leftover פסח cannot need bread when a real פסח does not, so the פסח does not take on the bread requirement.

steps.title: But a leftover פסח does need libations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the reasoning of step 12. A real פסח needs no libations, yet a leftover פסח that becomes a שלמים does need them. So 'the real thing does not need it' cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same question applies now too: is there anything where a פסח itself does not need libations, but its leftover does need libations?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave about bread. It points out that the same reasoning would give a wrong result about libations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said: a real פסח needs no bread, so a leftover פסח cannot need bread. But we already accept that a leftover פסח, once it is a שלמים, needs libations like any שלמים, even though a real פסח never has libations. That shows the leftover can need something the real פסח does not, so the reasoning of step 12 breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge built on what was just said
Libations: the wine and flour offerings that come with many קרבנות, including a שלמים
A leftover פסח: a פסח animal that was not used on time

phrases.english: If so, now too:
is there anything
where the פסח itself does not need libations,
but its leftover needs libations?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rhetorical answer of step 12 by applying the same reasoning to libations.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning in step 12 that a leftover פסח cannot need bread because a real פסח does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Libations show that a leftover פסח can need something a real פסח does not need, so comparing it to the real פסח proves nothing.

steps.title: The real comparison is a leftover תודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what it meant. It was not comparing to a real פסח. It was comparing to a leftover תודה: if a leftover תודה brings no bread, a leftover from a different kind of offering surely brings no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we are saying: is there anything where a leftover תודה itself does not need bread, but a leftover that comes from some other kind of offering does need bread?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies its earlier answer. The comparison is between one leftover and another leftover, not between a leftover and a real פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leftover תודה is offered without bread. A leftover פסח slaughtered for the sake of a תודה should not be stricter than that. So it needs no bread, and the libations question no longer applies, because the proof never depended on what a real פסח needs.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying: the גמרא explains what its earlier words really meant
A leftover תודה: an extra תודה animal that is no longer the main offering
Bread: the loaves that normally come with a תודה
From elsewhere: here, from a different kind of offering

steps.whatToRemember: A leftover פסח slaughtered for the sake of a תודה needs no bread. A leftover תודה itself brings no bread, and an outside leftover cannot be stricter.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
is there anything

phrases.aramaic: דְּמוֹתַר תּוֹדָה עַצְמָהּ – לָא בָּעֵי לֶחֶם,
phrases.english: where a leftover תודה itself does not need bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ מוֹתָר דְּאָתְיָא לְהוּ מֵעָלְמָא – בָּעֲיָא לֶחֶם?!
phrases.english: but a leftover that comes to them from elsewhere needs bread?!
phrases.notes: 'From elsewhere' means a leftover from another kind of offering, like our leftover פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן הָכִי קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by restating what step 12 meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the earlier answer: the comparison is to a leftover תודה, not to a real פסח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 12 seemed to argue that a leftover can never need what the real פסח does not need.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument compares leftover to leftover. A leftover תודה needs no bread, so a leftover פסח slaughtered as a תודה needs none either.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is about a leftover אשם
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בריה דרב הילל asks how we know that the פסוק about a שלמים from the flock is speaking of a leftover פסח. It might be speaking of a leftover אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר son of רב הילל objected: from where do we know that the פסוק is written about a leftover פסח? Maybe it is written about a leftover אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the source that teaches a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים. רב יימר questions whether that פסוק is really speaking about a פסח at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'if his offering is from the flock' was used for a leftover פסח, which comes only from the flock. But an אשם also comes only from the flock. So the פסוק could just as easily be speaking about a leftover אשם, and then we would lose our source for the leftover פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it: a sage raises a strong challenge
From where: how do we know
Maybe: introduces another possibility
A guilt offering: it also comes only from the flock

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב [יֵימַר] בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הִילֵּל:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar, son of Rav Hillel, objected to it:
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is written about a leftover פסח?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק 'And if his offering is from the flock,' quoted in the next step.

phrases.english: Maybe it is written about a leftover אשם!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יֵימַר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הִילֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question about the פסוק that is the source for a leftover פסח becoming a שלמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'from the flock' in ויקרא 3:6 as a source for a leftover פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אשם is also only from the flock, so the פסוק could be speaking about a leftover אשם instead.

steps.title: 'From the flock' means any kind of flock
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the wording of the פסוק. 'From the flock' means an animal that can come from every kind of flock, sheep or goats. A פסח can come from either, but an אשם comes only from rams.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the פסוק says, 'And if his offering for a שלמים is from the flock.' This means something that is equal across the whole flock.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the source by reading the exact words of the פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'from' with 'the flock' points to an animal that can be any kind of flock animal, a sheep or a goat. That matches a פסח, which may be a lamb or a kid. An אשם must be a ram, so the פסוק cannot be speaking about a leftover אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A peace offering
Flock: sheep and goats
Something equal: here, an animal that can come equally from sheep or goats

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'if his offering is from the flock for a שלמים' teaches about a leftover פסח, because a פסח can come from sheep or goats. An אשם comes only from rams.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"And if his offering is from the flock
for a sacrifice of peace offerings":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:6

phrases.english: something that is equal across all the flock.
phrases.notes: He means an animal that can be a sheep or a goat. A פסח can be either, but an אשם is only a ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יימר's challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the פסוק's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might be speaking about a leftover אשם, since an אשם also comes only from the flock.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From the flock' means an animal that can come from all kinds of flock. That fits a פסח and not an אשם, which comes only from rams.

steps.title: רבי אבין: the word 'from' usually leaves things out
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין בר חייא (or רבי אבין בר כהנא) objects to רבא. Everywhere else the word מן is read as leaving something out, yet here רבא read it as including every kind of flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר חייא, and some say רבי אבין בר כהנא, objected: Everywhere you say that the word 'from' comes to leave something out, and here you say 'from' comes to include?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין challenges the way רבא read the פסוק in step 16. He says the word מן normally means 'only part of', so it should point to an offering that comes from only part of the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said 'from the flock' means an animal that can come from every kind of flock, so it fits a פסח. רבי אבין turns this around: מן usually narrows things down. Read that way, 'from the flock' fits an אשם better, since an אשם comes only from rams.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; a strong challenge against what was just said
From; often read as 'only part of'
To leave out; to exclude
To include; to add more cases

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Chiya objected to this,
and some say it was Rabbi Avin bar Kahana:
Everywhere you say 'from' comes to leave out,
and here 'from' comes to include?!
phrases.notes: He means רבא's reading in step 16, that 'from the flock' covers both sheep and goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading of מן הצאן from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'from the flock' means an animal from every kind of flock, which fits a פסח and not an אשם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everywhere else מן narrows things down. So 'from the flock' should mean only part of the flock, which points to an אשם (rams only) and not a פסח.

steps.title: רבי מני: here too 'from' leaves things out
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני answers that מן does leave something out here too. A פסח cannot be in its second year and cannot be female.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: Here too 'from' comes to leave out. A פסח does not come from an animal in its second year, and it does not come from a female.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני defends רבא. He agrees that מן leaves something out, but says it leaves out older animals and females, not one of the kinds of flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מן keeps its usual job of narrowing, so there is no clash with the rule everywhere else. What is left out is age and gender, not sheep or goats. So 'from the flock' can still mean both sheep and goats, which fits a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same rule applies here
An animal in its second year
A female animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said:
Here too, 'from' comes to leave out:
that it does not come as an animal in its second year,
and it does not come as a female.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי הָכָא נָמֵי ״מִן״ לְהוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבין's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the word keeps its usual narrowing meaning, but it narrows something else (age and gender).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מן always narrows, 'from the flock' must mean only some kinds of flock, so it would be an אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: מן narrows by leaving out second-year animals and females. Both sheep and goats are still included, so the פסוק fits a פסח.

steps.title: רב חנא: 'if a lamb, if a goat' shows it is not about a פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה asks: the later פסוקים say 'if a lamb' and 'if a goat'. If the section were about a leftover פסח, these words would not be needed, since we already know a פסח comes from both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בגדתאה objected: Can you really say that this פסוק is written about a leftover פסח? From the fact that it is written 'if a lamb' and 'if a goat', we learn that it is not written about a leftover פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to the whole idea that the פסוק speaks of a leftover פסח. רב חנא points to the next פסוקים, which spell out a lamb and a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already taught in another place that a פסח can be a lamb or a goat. If this section were about a פסח, the words 'if a lamb' and 'if a goat' would teach nothing new. So רב חנא says the section must be about a regular שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח, which is offered as a שלמים
Can you really say...? (a sign of a strong question)
A lamb
A goat
By implication; we learn from this that

phrases.english: Rav Chana of Baghdad objected to this:
Can you really say

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי כְּתִיב הַאי – בְּמוֹתַר פֶּסַח כְּתִיב?!
phrases.english: that when this is written, it is written about a leftover פסח?!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the פסוק about a שלמים 'from the flock' (ויקרא 3:6).

phrases.english: But from the fact that it is written 'if a lamb,' 'if a goat,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:7 and 3:12.

phrases.english: we learn that it is not written about a leftover פסח!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי מני's answer, a new challenge attacks the basic claim that the section is about a leftover פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (from steps 15-16) that the פסוק about a שלמים 'from the flock' speaks of a leftover פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. A פסח is already known to come from lambs or goats, so 'if a lamb' and 'if a goat' would be extra if the section were about a פסח.

steps.title: The word 'lamb' is needed for the tail of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that those words are needed for something else, taught in a ברייתא. The word 'lamb' teaches that the tail of a פסח is burned on the מזבח, like the tail of a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'Lamb' comes to include the פסח in the rule of the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the claim that the section is about a leftover פסח. The words that looked extra are really teaching a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנא said 'if a lamb' teaches nothing new for a פסח. The answer is that it does teach something new: a lamb's fat tail must be burned on the מזבח as with a שלמים, and the פסח is included in this rule. Since the words have their own job, they do not prove that the section is not about a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
Like what was taught in a ברייתא
A lamb (same word as כשב, with the letters switched)
The fat tail of a sheep, burned on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that 'from the flock' speaks of a leftover פסח holds up. מן still narrows, leaving out second-year animals and females. The words 'if a lamb' are not extra, because they teach that a פסח's tail goes on the מזבח.

phrases.english: That is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
'Lamb' comes to include the פסח for the tail.
phrases.notes: The rule that the tail is offered on the מזבח appears in ויקרא 3:9.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנא's challenge from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassignment: the words that seemed extra are needed for a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'If a lamb' and 'if a goat' would be extra for a פסח, so the section must be about a regular שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Lamb' teaches that the tail of a פסח is offered on the מזבח, so the words are not extra and the section can still be about a leftover פסח.

steps.title: 'If a lamb' gives a leftover פסח all the rules of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The words 'if a lamb' include a פסח whose first year has passed, and שלמים brought because of a פסח, in all the rules of שלמים: סמיכה, נסכים, and waving the breast and thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'if a lamb', it comes to include a פסח that has passed its first year, and שלמים that come because of a פסח. They get every rule of שלמים: they need סמיכה, נסכים, and the waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 20 keeps going and learns another rule from the words 'if a lamb'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be in its first year. Once it is older it cannot be a פסח, and it is brought as a שלמים instead. The ברייתא says it is a full שלמים in every way, with all the usual שלמים procedures.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסח animal that is now past its first year, so it is too old to be a פסח
שלמים that are brought because of a פסח, such as a leftover פסח animal
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
The flour, oil, and wine offerings that go along with a קרבן
Waving the breast and the thigh of the שלמים

phrases.english: When it says: 'If a lamb'
phrases.notes: This is another phrase from the same section of פסוקים about שלמים in ויקרא 3.

phrases.english: it is to include a פסח whose year has passed;
and שלמים that come because of a פסח
in all the rules of שלמים,
that they require leaning of hands and נסכים
and waving of the breast and thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אִם כֶּבֶשׂ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח past its first year, and שלמים that come because of a פסח, are full שלמים with סמיכה, נסכים, and waving of breast and thigh.

steps.title: 'If a goat' starts a new topic: no tail for a goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends. 'If a goat' breaks off the topic, so the tail rule does not carry over to a goat. A goat's tail is not burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'if a goat', it breaks off the topic. This teaches that a goat does not need its tail burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining why 'if a goat' is written: it stops the earlier rules about the tail from applying to goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules learned from 'lamb' (step 20) might have spread to every animal in the section. Starting over with 'if a goat' shows that the tail rule stays with sheep, so a goat's tail is not one of the parts burned.

keyTerms.meaning: It broke off the topic, so the earlier rule does not carry forward
The fat tail of a sheep, which is burned on the מזבח in a שלמים
A goat

phrases.english: When it says: 'If a goat'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:12

phrases.english: it broke off the topic,
teaching about the goat
that it does not require the tail.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns three things from the שלמים section: a פסח's tail is burned like a שלמים, a leftover פסח gets all the rules of שלמים, and a goat's tail is not burned.
steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אִם עֵז״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat brought as a שלמים does not need its tail burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: Isn't this already learned from אבוה דשמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs 'if a lamb' to teach that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים. אבוה דשמואל already learns this from 'if his offering is from the flock'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we really learn it from here? We learn it from אבוה דשמואל. He said: 'And if his offering for a שלמים is from the flock' means that something brought from the flock, the פסח, becomes a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The rule it learns from 'if a lamb' already has a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דשמואל reads 'from the flock' as pointing to an animal that comes only from the flock, which is the פסח. The פסוק then says it becomes a שלמים. If that teaching already exists, the ברייתא's reading of 'if a lamb' seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it learned from here?
A שלמים offering

phrases.english: But is it derived from here?!
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.

phrases.english: It is derived from Shmuel's father,
for Shmuel's father said:
'And if his offering for a שלמים sacrifice is from the flock'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:6

phrases.english: something that comes from the flock
shall be a שלמים sacrifice!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of 'if a lamb' as the source that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: אבוה דשמואל already learns the same rule from a different phrase, so the ברייתא's source seems unneeded.

steps.title: Even אבוה דשמואל's source seems unneeded, because of רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. Even without the ברייתא, אבוה דשמואל's reading is extra, because רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה learns the rule from 'flock and herd' in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, it is learned from what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה. He said: Where do we learn that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים? The פסוק says, 'You shall slaughter the פסח to ה׳ your G-d, flock and herd.' But a פסח comes only from sheep and goats! So this teaches that a leftover פסח becomes an offering that can come from flock and herd. What is that? שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds to its question. A third source teaches the same rule, so the problem of extra פסוקים gets worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח can never be brought from cattle, so 'and herd' cannot be about the פסח itself. רבה בר אבוה says it describes what a leftover פסח turns into: an offering that can come from cattle as well, which is שלמים. Now the same rule has three sources, and the גמרא must explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: And still: the problem remains or grows
A leftover פסח animal that was not used as a פסח
Flock (sheep and goats) and herd (cattle)
What is it?

steps.confusionAlert: 'צאן ובקר' does not mean a פסח can be brought from cattle. It cannot. That is exactly why the words are read as being about the leftover פסח becoming a שלמים.

phrases.english: But still, from what רב נחמן
said in the name of רבה בר אבוה it is derived!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
From where do we know that a leftover פסח is offered as a שלמים?
As it says: 'You shall slaughter the פסח to Hashem your G-d,
flock and herd.'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:2

phrases.english: But doesn't a פסח come
only from sheep and from goats!
Rather, from here we learn about the leftover פסח

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא לְדָבָר הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן וּמִן הַבָּקָר;
phrases.english: that it should be for something that comes from flock and from herd;
and what is that? שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 23's question by showing that even אבוה דשמואל's source is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבוה דשמואל's reading of 'from the flock' (and also the ברייתא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: a third source, 'צאן ובקר' in דברים, already teaches that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים.

steps.title: Answer begins: three פסוקים are written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. Three separate פסוקים really are written about this, so each must be teaching something of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, three פסוקים are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to steps 23–24. It is setting up the next move, where it will explain what each of the three פסוקים is needed for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not drop any of the three sources. It accepts that all three exist, which means none can be extra. Each one must teach a different part of the law about a פסח brought as a שלמים.

phrases.english: Rather, three פסוקים are written,

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of the גמרא: if a פסוק looks extra, it must be teaching something new.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תְּלָתָא קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי

steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source is needed for its own purpose (to be spelled out next).

steps.terutzMaskana: All three פסוקים are needed, and each teaches its own detail.
